newsitem.title: INDIA: India postal, phone strike to continue next week.
newsitem.headline: India postal, phone strike to continue next week.

text.p: Indian trade unions said on Saturday that a four-day-old strike by one million postal and telephone department employees will continue at least until Tuesday, when the federal cabinet is expected to meet.

"The strike will continue until the 29th, till the cabinet meets and decides favourably. It is in the hands of government," P.L. Dua, a senior official of the National Federation of Telecom Employees, a leading union, told Reuters.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda is scheduled to be travelling outside Delhi until Tuesday, when a cabinet meeting has been tentatively scheduled.

The unions have rejected a government promise to consider their demand for the elimination of a 3,500-rupee ($100) ceiling on annual pay bonuses, arguing that a ceiling on bonuses for rail workers had already been lifted and set a precedent.
The ceiling was imposed as an austerity measure by the federal government earlier this year.
Millions of letters have piled up as a result of the strike by six unions, three of them representing postal unions.

Three other unions representing telecommunication employees have stopped manual services like repairs and billing in telephone exchanges but most telephones are working because they work on automated exchanges.

Although Communications Minister Beni Prasad Varma was sympathetic to the demands of labour unions, nothing less than a cabinet decision in favour of the unions' demands could force the strikers to return to work, Dua said.
"The minister is favourable. But without fulfilment of our demands we will not come back," he said. "There is no question of talks. It is a policy matter to be settled by the cabinet."
Government officials were not available for comment.
An unknown number of army experts have been helping telecommunications and postal services for the past three days.
On Friday, the federation had said they expected the strike to be called off soon, perhaps later in the day.
But unions said verbal assurances that the cabinet would decide in their favour were not enough.

A government official told Reuters on Friday that negotiations had stalled on union demands that striking employees be paid for days missed during the strike, while the government wanted them to forego leave in return.
The Communications Ministry had declared the strike as illegal on the day it began, saying sufficient notice had not been given by the unions.
But Varma and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram quickly sought to make peace with the unions, saying they deserved a sympathetic hearing.
